items.claim: Claude's consumer plans are now Free ($0), Pro ($20/month), Max ($100/month) and Ultra ($200/month). Ultra takes the old $200 Max 20x slot.
items.why_it_matters: If you pay for Claude Code through a subscription, the tier names and prices you budget around have changed.
items.try_this: Open claude.com/pricing and check which tier your current plan maps to before your next renewal.

verification.method: Claude pricing page lists Max at $100 and Ultra at $200 per month

items.claim: On the Ultra plan, verified accounts have no 5-hour usage limit. The video says weekly limits stay in place.
items.why_it_matters: Long agent runs on Ultra no longer stall at the 5-hour window, but only once your account counts as verified.
items.try_this: On Ultra, check Settings > Usage. Theo says verified accounts no longer show a 'Current session' bar.

verification.method: Pricing page footnote on Ultra says no 5-hour limit for verified accounts; weekly-limit detail not checked

items.claim: BootLoops, from Harvard physicist Matthew Schwartz, is an open-source harness of exact-calculation tools and agent skills for quantitative science. Its GitHub org has 7 public repos, mostly MIT-licensed, including a skills repo packaged as Claude Code and Codex plugins.
items.why_it_matters: It is a public example of a domain-specific harness and skill set built for any model doing long, checkable research work.
items.try_this: Browse the BootLoops-ai skills repo on GitHub and read its research protocols as a model for your own agent skills.

verification.method: bootloops.ai and GitHub org list open-source repos and licenses; code not run

items.excerpt: a harness to help Large Language Models do interdisciplinary quantitative science

items.claim: T3 Code merged PR #28410 on Nov 2, 2026. Claude processes it starts now report CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT as t3-code instead of the Agent SDK default sdk-ts.
items.why_it_matters: Apps are relabeling their entrypoint to avoid how usage may be weighted. The linked issue warns this hides the label and may conflict with Anthropic's terms.

verification.method: PR page shows merged Nov 2, 2026 with entrypoint change; not run

items.claim: Manus 2.0, announced Sept 28, 2026, adds the Cascade agent harness, Automations that start from events such as a new email or calendar event, and an always-on Cloud Computer. Video Editor followed on Oct 1.
items.why_it_matters: Event-triggered agents that run on persistent hosted machines are now a packaged feature, not something you have to build yourself.
items.try_this: Read the Manus 2.0 post to see which connected services Automations can trigger on before designing a workflow.

verification.method: Manus blog confirms 2.0 features and dates; Cascade parallel sub-agents not confirmed

items.excerpt: Manus 2.0 is here, with the new Cascade agent harness, Cloud Computer and Automations

items.claim: Anthropic says protein design and other dual-use biology research features are not available for general access in Claude Fable 5. It plans an access program for scientists, and Opus 5 remains its most capable generally available model.
items.why_it_matters: Biology builders should expect refusals or blocks on the newest model and plan around Opus 5 or a future trusted access program.
items.excerpt: protein design and other dual-use research biology capabilities remain unavailable for general access in Claude Fable 5.

items.claim: OpenAI published Codex CLI pre-releases rust-v0.167.0-alpha.2 and alpha.3 on GitHub on Nov 1, 2026. The release pages include no changelog notes.
items.why_it_matters: A 0.167.0 Codex release appears close. Wait for stable notes before upgrading production setups.

items.claim: To run many long Claude Code projects at once, Schwartz used one session per project and a master session that coordinates the others. Background subagents meant a classifier block stopped only one agent, and periodic file consolidation helped against context loss from compaction.
items.why_it_matters: These are practical patterns for multi-day agent work: isolating failures, a coordinator session, and files as durable memory across compaction.
items.try_this: Add a step to long agent tasks that has the agent consolidate its notes into one up-to-date plan file at regular intervals.
items.excerpt: a master session that coordinates the others, allocates compute, and validates results

items.claim: In Vibe Physics (first published March 2026), Schwartz had Claude Code keep a tree of markdown files with one summary per stage and one file per task. He also cross-checked its work with GPT and Gemini and added a CLAUDE.md rule banning skipped steps.
items.why_it_matters: These are simple, reusable ways to cut silent errors and lost context when an agent works through a long technical project.
items.try_this: Add to CLAUDE.md: never use phrases like 'this becomes' to skip steps; show the calculation or say 'I don't know'.
items.excerpt: It works better with things it can look up than things it has to remember.

items.claim: Ray Fu published a free guide to building a multi-agent stock research team in Manus, with Analyst, Quant, Risk and Report agents. Its triggers include earnings dates, newsletters and CEO posts on X.
items.why_it_matters: The guide exists, but its trading usefulness is unproven and its X-monitoring trigger raises platform terms concerns.

verification.method: Guide exists; trading value not assessed; X-post trigger not confirmed in Manus docs

items.claim: Anthropic reports that Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8 designed protein binders that worked against 14 of 15 targets in outside wet-lab tests. Hit rates were 22.6% to 35.1%, against a typical 10-15%.
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete public test of an agent running a long, multi-model science pipeline on its own, and the prompts and data are released.
items.try_this: Read the released 30,000-token protein design prompt to see how Anthropic set up a 48-hour autonomous agent session.

verification.method: Post exists and states these figures; wet-lab results are Anthropic's report, not independently checked

items.excerpt: Claude (Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8) designed protein binders against 15 targets, and succeeded against 14 of them.

items.claim: Anthropic says Claude Opus 5 in Claude Science took raw proprietary NMR and LC-MS instrument files and a short prompt, with no vendor software. It returned results in 23 and 19 minutes, with purity 96.4% versus the lab's 96.33%.
items.why_it_matters: It suggests a generally available model can decode undocumented binary formats and do routine lab analysis, with self-checks against the file's own totals.
items.try_this: In Claude Science, give Claude a raw NMR or LC-MS file and ask it to confirm the compound's identity and purity.

verification.method: Post exists and states timings and purity match; single-sample result reported by Anthropic
